meta.parties: Appuhamy Et. Al. v. The Doloswala Tea and Rubber Company

rules.statement: A lessee is not entitled to claim compensation for improvements made by him in respect of land leased for ninety-nine years, unless the lessor also claims such compensation.
rules.supporting_quote: "The Roman-Dutch law gives to the improver of lands a right to compensation for improvements effected by him, and with this right goes the farther right to retain possession until compensation is paid. But this right is given only to a person who, at the time when he made the improvements in respect of which the right is claimed, had the possessio civilis, which is defined as 'deteniio animo domini.' A lessee has no such possession."
